hero.title: Build your club. Own every decision.

report.intro: Thanks to the {{weather}} weather, a crowd of {{attendance}} gathered to watch the match. {{referee}} was the referee, assisted by {{assistant1}} and {{assistant2}}.
kickoff: Everyone is ready - the match is about to begin!
The ball is rolling between {{home}} and {{away}}. Let the show begin!
The captains shake hands, the referee checks the watch... and we're under way!
A big-match atmosphere for {{home}} against {{away}}. Here we go!
Kick-off. {{home}} and {{away}} have a lot riding on this one.
And we're off! Get comfortable: this one looks promising.
First whistle and the first sprints. {{home}} and {{away}}, face to face with everything to play for.
report.fullTime: The referee blows the whistle for full time.

goalless: Half time: 0-0 and everything still to play for.
Goalless at the break. Time for a team talk.
End of the first half: lots of running, few chances, no goals.
Half time with nothing on the board. The second half needs to be something else.
level: Level at the break ({{score}}). Wide open.
We reach the interval at {{score}}. Long may the fun continue.
homeLeads: {{home}} go in at the break ahead: {{score}}.
{{home}} head for the dressing room in front ({{score}}). {{away}} have homework to do.
awayLeads: At the interval, {{away}} are in front: {{score}}.
{{away}} head for the dressing room ahead ({{score}}). {{home}} have homework to do.

goallessDraw: Full time: 0-0. Neither side found a way through.
It ends goalless. The goalkeepers win this one.
scoringDraw: Full time: {{score}}. Goals and drama shared out.
The final whistle goes with the sides level ({{score}}). Nobody got bored.
That's it: {{home}} {{score}} {{away}}. Nothing to separate them.
homeWin: Full time! {{home}} win {{score}} and their fans love it.
Final whistle. {{home}} get the job done: {{score}}.
awayWin: Full time! {{away}} win {{score}} and take the match.
Final whistle. {{away}} come away with the win: {{score}}.
bigWin: Final whistle on a day {{winner}} will remember for a long time: {{score}}.

ratings.title: Player ratings
ratings.help: A rating starts at 6.0 and adds the player's contribution to his zone against the rival's (the same figure the engine uses to decide who wins each zone), his goals, cards and injuries, and the result scaled by the minutes he played. Under 10 minutes he is not rated (N/R). Tap a rating to see its breakdown.
ratings.contributionHint: The player's average contribution to his zone against the rival's in the opposing duel

match.stadiumEntry: {{home}} and {{away}} take to the pitch at {{stadium}}!
match.noNotableEvents: No notable events in this match.

goal: It's in! {{player}} is clean through, looks up, picks a spot... and {{keeper}} can't reach it.
GOOOAL! {{player}} gets {{team}} on the scoresheet with a crisp strike.
What a goal from {{player}}! One touch to control, one to set, and a rocket into the top corner.
Goal for {{team}}! A pinpoint cross and {{player}} heads it home; {{keeper}} doesn't move.
{{player}} spins and shoots on the turn - it surprises everyone, {{keeper}} included!
GOAL! A move straight off the training ground, finished by {{player}} into an empty net.
In it goes! {{player}} pounces on a loose ball in the box and makes no mistake.
What a strike from {{player}}! It hugs the post on its way in and {{keeper}} can only watch.
{{player}} slaloms between two {{opponent}} defenders and slots it home. Lovely stuff.
Chipped! Out rushes {{keeper}} and {{player}} lifts it over the top. Goal for {{team}}!
Goal! {{player}} fires it in from close range and the {{opponent}} net is still shaking.
Lethal counter from {{team}}! {{player}} races half the length of the pitch and finishes past {{keeper}}.
noGoal: {{player}} goes close for {{team}}, but it's off target!
Chance for {{team}}! {{player}}'s effort is gathered comfortably by {{keeper}}.
So close! {{player}} can't quite find the corner.
{{player}} tries their luck from distance, but {{keeper}} gathers at the second attempt.
Off the post! {{player}}'s effort crashes against the woodwork. Unlucky for {{team}}!
What a save! Full stretch from {{keeper}} to keep out {{player}}'s shot.
{{player}} is through on {{keeper}}... and blazes it over the bar.
A header from {{player}} skims the top of the crossbar. Ooh!
{{player}} tries one trick too many and the {{opponent}} defence picks their pocket.
{{player}}'s cross-shot rolls agonisingly across the face of goal with nobody there to tap it in.
{{team}} had to score there! {{player}} shoots from point-blank range and {{keeper}} saves with a foot.
{{player}} lets fly from outside the box... closer to the corner flag than the goal.
A gorgeous volley from {{player}}, tipped away by {{keeper}} with a save for the highlights reel.
One on one for {{player}}... and {{keeper}} wins it, narrowing the angle perfectly.
yellowCard: Yellow card for {{player}} after a late challenge.
Booked! {{player}} handles the ball to stop a {{opponent}} counter.
{{player}} arrives late and the referee doesn't hesitate: yellow card.
A yellow for {{player}}, who is now walking a tightrope.
{{player}} loses their cool and is shown a yellow. Every tackle counts from here.
{{player}} is booked for diving. The referee wasn't buying it.
Yellow card for {{player}} for wasting time at a throw-in.
redCard: {{player}} is sent off! {{team}} are down to ten.
Red card! {{player}}'s afternoon is over, and it's a long walk to the tunnel.
Straight red for {{player}} after a reckless tackle. {{team}} are in trouble now.
Sent off! {{player}} leaves {{team}} a player short, and their manager can't believe it.
No hesitation from the referee: red card, and {{player}} is off.
Red for {{player}}! {{team}} will have to dig in with a player fewer.
{{player}} brings down a {{opponent}} attacker who was through on goal and sees a straight red.
injury: {{player}} is down and looks in pain. Worry for {{team}}.
{{player}} has to come off injured, applauded by the crowd.
{{player}} clutches a thigh after a sprint. That doesn't look good.
The physios are on: {{player}} has hurt an ankle.
{{player}} limps off asking for a change. Grim faces on the {{team}} bench.
An accidental collision leaves {{player}} on the turf. They won't be able to carry on.
substitution: {{team}} make a change: {{outPlayer}} makes way for {{inPlayer}}.
Movement on the {{team}} bench: {{inPlayer}} comes on for {{outPlayer}}.
{{outPlayer}} off, {{inPlayer}} on. The {{team}} manager makes a move.
Substitution for {{team}}: {{inPlayer}} bounds onto the pitch; {{outPlayer}} heads off.
That's the afternoon done for {{outPlayer}}. {{inPlayer}} takes their place.
Tactical change from {{team}}: off goes {{outPlayer}}, on comes {{inPlayer}}.
{{inPlayer}} finishes warming up, high-fives {{outPlayer}} and is into the action.
Change for {{team}}: {{outPlayer}} leaves the pitch and {{inPlayer}} picks up the baton.
abandoned: {{team}} can no longer field enough players to continue - the match is abandoned, and {{opponent}} are awarded the win.
With too few players left on the pitch, {{team}}'s match is called off - {{opponent}} take it 3-0.
The referee abandons the match: {{team}} are down to too few players to carry on, and {{opponent}} are awarded a 3-0 win.
defaultResult: The match could not be played: it is recorded as a 0-0 default result between {{team}} and {{opponent}}.
No match today: {{team}} and {{opponent}} are given a 0-0 by default.
penaltyGoal: PENALTY! {{player}} sends {{keeper}} the wrong way and scores for {{team}}!
{{player}} steps up and converts the penalty for {{team}}. Nothing {{keeper}} could do.
Cool as you like! {{player}} tucks the spot-kick into the top corner.
GOAL from the spot! {{player}} makes no mistake for {{team}}.
Short run-up, steely stare... and {{player}} chips it down the middle, Panenka-style. Nerves of steel!
{{player}} looks one way, {{keeper}} guesses right... but can't reach it. Goal for {{team}}!
Hit with real power by {{player}}: high into the net, and {{keeper}} has no chance.
penaltyMiss: PENALTY SAVED! It's kept out by {{keeper}}, who reads {{player}}'s spot-kick perfectly.
{{player}} steps up for {{team}}... and {{keeper}} keeps it out!
Disaster from the spot! {{player}}'s penalty sails off into the night.
Off the post! {{player}} hits the upright from the spot and {{team}} come away with nothing.
{{player}} tries a Panenka... and {{keeper}} simply stands still and catches it. Ouch.
{{player}} blazes the penalty over. That ball is still climbing.
Saved by {{keeper}}! A cat-like dive to deny {{player}} from twelve yards.
freeKickGoal: WHAT A FREE KICK! {{player}} bends it over the wall and {{keeper}} never sees it.
{{player}} strikes the free kick for {{team}} and it's in! All {{keeper}} can do is watch.
GOAL! A direct free kick from {{player}} finds the corner for {{team}}!
A dipping free kick from {{player}}! It drops like a stone just under the bar.

matchSchedule.title: Match schedule
matchSchedule.description: Sets which days and what time league fixtures are dated on - e.g. Saturdays at 14:00, or every day at 16:00. Saving also re-dates the unplayed matches of every league without its own schedule (in all countries), starting from the next slot after now. To re-date just one country, use "Reschedule fixtures" in the Countries section.

promotionRelegation.title: Promotion & relegation
promotionRelegation.description: How many teams move between adjacent tiers at the end of each season. Set either to 0 to turn that direction off entirely. Only affects a season rollover that hasn't happened yet.

maxFriendlies.title: Friendly matches
maxFriendlies.description: Maximum friendly matches a team may accept per calendar week (Monday to Sunday). Set to 0 to turn friendlies off entirely.

friendlySchedule.title: Friendly match days

offerNegotiationWindow.title: Offer negotiation window

help.title: Help & how to play
help.subtitle: Everything you need to know about running your club, from claiming a team to lifting the cup.

items.q: How do I open Striker in my browser?
items.a: Open Chrome, Safari, Edge or Firefox and go to https://striker.example.com. Sign in with your Google account. You don't need to install anything to play: the website works the same in any browser.

items.q: Can I have it as an app on my phone?
items.a: Yes. Striker can be installed on your phone's home screen: it opens full screen, without the browser bar, and has its own icon, just like any other app.

items.q: How do I install it on Android?
items.a: In Chrome, go to striker.example.com, tap the menu (the three dots in the top corner) and choose "Install app" or "Add to Home screen". Confirm with "Install" and the icon will appear on your home screen.

items.q: How do I install it on iPhone or iPad?
items.a: Open the website in Safari, tap the Share button (the square with an arrow pointing up), scroll down the list and choose "Add to Home Screen". Then tap "Add" in the top right.

items.q: What about on a computer?
items.a: In Chrome or Edge, click the install icon on the right side of the address bar, or open the menu and choose "Install Striker". It opens in its own window, without tabs or a browser bar.

items.q: Do notifications work with the installed app?
items.a: Yes. Turn them on from the bell in the header and your browser will ask for permission. On iPhone and iPad, notifications only arrive if the app is installed on the home screen (iOS 16.4 or later).

items.q: Does it work offline?
items.a: No. Striker needs an internet connection, because live matches, the transfer market and your alerts change constantly and are always loaded from the server. The installed app is just a shortcut, with no offline features.

items.q: How do I uninstall it?
items.a: Like any app: press and hold its icon and choose "Uninstall" or "Remove from Home screen". Your account and your club are not deleted, because they are stored on the server.

items.q: How do I start playing?
items.a: Sign in with your Google account, then pick a country. You're assigned an open team in that country, starting from the top division down, so you always begin with the best available club.

items.q: Can I choose which team I get?
items.a: No - you get whichever unowned team is open in the country you picked. Every division fills from the top tier downward.

items.q: Can I rename my team?
items.a: Yes, once, from the dashboard. Names must be between 2 and 50 characters.

items.q: What's the goal of the game?
items.a: Build your club over an ongoing series of seasons: win matches, earn promotion, manage your finances, develop your squad, and chase silverware in the cup competitions.

items.q: What does the dashboard show me?
items.a: Your next match and last result, your top scorer, head-to-head history against your next opponent, your friend-group rank, and quick links to your squad, finances, and lineup.

items.q: What are those alert banners for?
items.a: The dashboard flags anything that needs your attention: contracts expiring at season end, players unavailable through injury or suspension, pending transfer offers and friendly challenges, and whether your budget is running low.

items.q: What is "Live around the world"?
items.a: A feed of matches other managers are currently playing live, anywhere in the game world. Pick one to watch it unfold, or ask for another suggestion.

items.q: How do I set my lineup?
items.a: Tap a player to pick them up, then tap a spot on the pitch or the bench to place them there. Every outfield slot must be filled before you can save.

items.q: What formations can I use?
items.a: Balanced (4-4-2), Defensive (5-3-2), Attacking (3-4-3), Wingers (4-3-3), Packed midfield (4-5-1), and Wing-backs (3-5-2). Each spreads your players across defense, midfield, and attack differently.

items.q: Do I need separate lineups for league/cup and friendly matches?
items.a: You can set one, but you don't have to - a friendly match falls back to your league/cup default lineup if you haven't set one specifically for friendlies. Planned substitutions are shared between both.

items.q: What are planned substitutions?
items.a: You can schedule a limited number of substitutions to happen automatically during a match, choosing who comes off, who comes on, and at what minute - useful for resting players or reacting to the clock without watching live.

items.q: When does the lineup lock?
items.a: Shortly before kickoff, so last-second changes can't sneak into a match that's about to start. Save your lineup ahead of time to be safe.

items.q: What if a starter is injured or suspended?
items.a: You can still save them in your default lineup, but they won't actually play in any match while unavailable - swap them out before the real kickoff.

items.q: How are matches played out?
items.a: Every match simulates live, minute by minute, with commentary, goals, cards, injuries, and substitutions appearing as they happen. You can follow along in real time or check back for the result afterward.

items.q: What decides who scores?
items.a: The simulation compares each team's attack on a flank against the opponent's defense on the mirrored flank plus their goalkeeper (and likewise for midfield) - never a zone against that same zone. The "Position battle" tab shows these matchups as the match unfolds.

items.q: What else can I check during or after a match?
items.a: Player ratings minute-by-minute, a full event timeline, both lineups, and a written match report summarizing chances, cards, and injuries.

items.q: When are matches scheduled?
items.a: League fixtures are dated on the days and kickoff time configured for your league (set by the admins), one matchday per game week.

items.q: How do I buy a player?
items.a: Buy a listed player outright at their asking price - the fee is deducted from your budget immediately.

items.q: How do I search for specific players on the market?
items.a: Besides filtering by age, price, position and overall rating, you can require a minimum in one specific skill (e.g. at least 70 shot) and a minimum number of international caps - available on transfers, loans and free agents alike.

items.q: How do transfer offers work?
items.a: From a player's page, or on a market listing, propose a fee to their club plus the wage and contract length you're offering the player. The player judges the personal terms on the spot, before their club ever sees the fee. An accepted offer needs to sit open for a minimum time first, so the seller has a chance to compare it against other offers before committing.

items.q: How do loans work?
items.a: Loans are free, with no transfer fee - list one of your players for loan, or take another team's player on loan for a set number of seasons. They return to their parent club automatically once the loan ends.

items.q: What are free agents?
items.a: Unowned players you can sign directly by proposing a wage and contract length. If they were released recently, their former club may be owed a transfer premium when you sign them.

items.q: What's the transfer window?
items.a: Listing, buying, and accepting loan or offer deals only work while the transfer window is open. It closes and reopens on a schedule set by the admins.

items.q: What happens if my budget is deep in debt?
items.a: Once your club is insolvent, buying, signing, and taking players on loan are all blocked until your budget recovers - but selling or releasing players stays available so you can dig yourself out.

items.q: How does the youth academy work?
items.a: Your academy periodically produces a prospect ready for promotion to the first team. You can only promote one at a time, and there's a cooldown before the next one becomes available.

items.q: What does a head coach do?
items.a: Hiring a head coach speeds up every player's development and raises the quality of prospects your academy produces. There's no signing fee, just their wage, and you can fire them back to the open market at any time.

items.q: How do players improve or decline?
items.a: After matches, players can develop - their skills shift up or down based on age, playing time, and coaching. Check the evolution page to see what changed for your squad this season.

items.q: How do contracts and renewals work?
items.a: Offer a wage and contract length; the player decides on the spot based on what they think they're worth and how many seasons they're willing to commit to. Releasing a player ends their contract immediately and they can't be brought back.

items.q: What is contract-negotiation intelligence?
items.a: Every player has a hidden negotiation intelligence, from Naive to Mastermind, which you learn once you have negotiated with him. A sharper player reacts more to his recent form (a raise when improving, more seasons when declining), keeps more of his wage in his last season (75% to 95%), asks more to leave on a pre-contract (5% to 20% above his usual wage) and gives up more wage for a low release clause (5% to 15%).

items.q: Do players age and retire?
items.a: Yes - every player ages over time, developing early in their career and declining as they approach retirement, so your squad needs constant refreshing through the academy and transfer market.

items.q: Where does my budget come from?
items.a: Ticket revenue, sponsorship payments, prize money, season ticket sales, merchandising, and any transfer fees you receive - weighed against wages, transfer spending, and stadium upgrades.

items.q: What are sponsor deals?
items.a: Each season you pick one of three deals: Steady pays the highest guaranteed amount every match with no bonus; Balanced pays a solid guaranteed amount plus a bonus for a win or draw; Performance pays the least guaranteed but the biggest bonus for a good result. You're locked into your choice for the season, and can switch again once it rolls over.

items.q: How do I expand my stadium?
items.a: Choose a new seat count within the allowed range. The cost is deducted immediately, and construction takes about a week before the extra capacity is ready.

items.q: What is stadium maintenance?
items.a: Every round your club pays an upkeep cost proportional to your stadium's size and upgrades - a bigger stadium earns more matchday revenue, but costs more to maintain too.

items.q: Can I change my ticket price?
items.a: Yes, from the finances page - it directly affects how much matchday revenue you earn per attendee.

items.q: What does the cash-flow forecast tell me?
items.a: Your estimated weekly income against your weekly wage bill, and roughly how many weeks it'll take to hit the debt ceiling if nothing changes - a heads-up before you actually go insolvent.

items.q: How is the game world organized?
items.a: Each country has several tiers, each tier split into groups (leagues) of teams. You can browse every country, tier, and league in the world from the Leagues page, including standings and squads - not just your own.

items.q: How does promotion and relegation work?
items.a: At the end of each season, a set number of teams move up from each group to the tier above, and a set number move down to the tier below - keeping every division competitive over time.

items.q: What do the standings columns mean?
items.a: Points, average, wins, draws, and losses, plus goals for and against - the usual league-table numbers, updated after every matchday.

items.q: Do more countries become available over time?
items.a: Yes, the administration periodically expands the catalog of playable countries - for example, Scotland, Wales, Ireland, Russia and the former Yugoslav republics were added recently.

items.q: How does the domestic cup work?
items.a: A straight knockout: quarterfinals, semifinals, and a final. If a tie is level after normal play, it's settled on penalties. A team can also get a bye through a round if the bracket doesn't fill evenly. Ties kick off at 17:00, the country's local time, one round a day.

items.q: What is the international cup?
items.a: A regional knockout competition between the league champions of the countries in a region. A new edition starts when every country in the region has crowned a new champion since the last one, or as soon as one country has finished two seasons, so a slower league never holds the rest back for long. At least two countries are needed. Each tie kicks off at 20:45, local time in the home side's country.

items.q: What's a friendly match?
items.a: A non-competitive match against another team - it has no effect on your league position and pays no ticket revenue, so it's a safe way to test tactics or just play more football.

items.q: How do I set one up?
items.a: Challenge a team directly (optionally proposing a kickoff time: on the hour, quarter past, half past or quarter to). They have to accept before it's scheduled, and there's a weekly limit on how many friendlies a team can accept, set by the admins.

items.q: What days can friendlies kick off on?
items.a: Whichever weekdays are enabled by the admins. An accepted challenge is scheduled as soon as possible, pushed forward to the next allowed day if needed.

items.q: What's the national teams page?
items.a: It shows the weekly friendlies between national teams and, once one is running, the national-team World Cup: its group stage and knockout bracket. It's a spectator feature - you don't manage the national team yourself.

items.q: How does a national team call up my players?
items.a: Each national team automatically calls up the best eligible players born in that country, regardless of which club they play for. If one of your players is called up and starts, your club gets a notification.

items.q: What are international caps?
items.a: How many friendlies and national-team World Cup matches a player has started for their country - another signal of their quality, shown on their profile and now available as a transfer-market filter too.

items.q: What are friend groups?
items.a: A private leaderboard between you and your friends' teams, ranked by budget. It's not a real league or competition - just bragging rights over the clubs you already manage.

items.q: How do I join or create one?
items.a: Create a group with a name to get an invite code, or join an existing group using a code someone shares with you. You can leave a group at any time, or delete one you created.

sections.title: 1. Who is responsible
paragraphs: The controller of your personal data is {{controllerName}}. For any question or request about your privacy, write to {{contactEmail}}.

sections.title: 2. What data we collect
paragraphs: From your Google account: your name and email address, and your profile picture, which is only shown to you.
What you choose in the game: your country, your language, your notification preferences, your friend groups and your club.
How you use the service: the time of your last activity (to apply the inactivity rules below) and, if you turn push notifications on, your browser's push subscription.
Game data about your club (squad, matches, finances, transfers) is not personal data about you, but it is linked to your account while you own the club.

sections.title: 3. Why we use it and on what legal basis
paragraphs: To create your account, sign you in and run the game you asked to play (performance of the contract).
To send you the notifications you enabled (your consent, which you can withdraw at any time in the notification settings).
To keep the service secure and to release clubs and erase accounts that are no longer used (our legitimate interest in running a fair game).

sections.title: 4. Who receives your data
paragraphs: Google, which handles the sign-in and receives the technical data of the sign-in request.
Our hosting provider, which stores the data on our behalf.
Your browser's push service (for example Google, Mozilla or Apple), only if you enable push notifications.
Other players never see your name or email. Members of a friend group you join see your name and your club's name; nobody sees your email.
We do not sell your data and we do not use it for advertising or profiling.

sections.title: 5. How long we keep it
paragraphs: A club whose owner has not been active for 60 days is released. The account is kept without a club.
An account with no activity for 365 days is erased automatically. We warn you in the app 14 days before.
When you delete your account, your name, email, language, notifications, preferences, push subscriptions and group memberships are erased immediately.
Server logs and backups are kept for at most 30 days.

sections.title: 6. Your rights
paragraphs: You can access, rectify, erase, restrict, object to the use of and port your data. On the Account page you can download all your data and delete your account yourself.
For anything else, write to {{contactEmail}}. We answer within one month.
You may also complain to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD, www.aepd.es) or to your local supervisory authority.

sections.title: 7. Cookies and browser storage
paragraphs: We only use what is strictly necessary for the service you asked for, so no consent banner is needed:
• Session cookie (jwt): keeps you signed in. HTTP-only, deleted when you sign out or after it expires.
• Theme and language preferences, stored in your browser, so the app looks the way you chose.
• Cookies set by Google's sign-in button while you sign in with Google.
We do not use analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.

sections.title: 8. Minimum age
paragraphs: Striker is for people aged 16 or over. You confirm it when you accept the terms.

sections.title: 9. Changes
paragraphs: If this policy changes in a way that matters, its version number changes and we ask you to accept it again.

sections.title: 1. Who may use Striker
paragraphs: Striker is a free football management game run by {{controllerName}}. You must be at least 16 years old. By accepting these terms you confirm it.

sections.title: 2. Your account and your club
paragraphs: You sign in with your Google account. You manage one club at a time. Your club and its data are game data: they have no monetary value and cannot be sold or exchanged outside the game.

sections.title: 3. Inactivity
paragraphs: A club whose owner has not signed in for 60 days is released and becomes a computer-managed club; you can get a new club when you come back. An account with no activity for 365 days is erased. We warn you in the app (and by push if enabled) beforehand.

sections.title: 4. Fair play
paragraphs: Do not use bots, exploit bugs on purpose, harass other players or choose club or group names that are offensive or impersonate others. We may rename a club or remove an account that breaks these rules.

sections.title: 5. Friend groups
paragraphs: Members of a friend group can see each other's names and clubs. If the owner of a group deletes their account, the group passes to the member who joined first, or is deleted if nobody else is in it.

sections.title: 6. Deleting your account
paragraphs: You can delete your account at any time from the Account page. Your club is released and your personal data is erased, as described in the Privacy Policy.

sections.title: 7. Availability
paragraphs: The game is provided as is, without guarantees. We may change it, interrupt it or reset parts of the game world, for example for maintenance.

sections.title: 8. Changes and contact
paragraphs: If these terms change in a way that matters, their version number changes and we ask you to accept them again. Questions: {{contactEmail}}.
